result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): no prior resolved match. Grepped docs/issues/*.yaml (219 files) for 'task_records|Ecto.Multi|SUB_PROCESS|sub_process|synchronous.completion|Multi key collision|merge Multi' (16 hits) and, more narrowly, for the exact function/error strings 'cannot merge Multi|found in both Ecto.Multi|append_sub_process_children_creation_multi|maybe_chain_synchronous_completion|append_start_multi' (1 hit: ISS-0392 itself). Of the 16 broad hits, 3 are status: resolved (ISS-0284, ISS-0278, ISS-0224); read all three in full -- ISS-0284 is unused-default-value compiler warnings in engine_sub_process_test.exs/sub_process_test.exs (unrelated defect class, files only incidentally overlap), ISS-0224 is SandboxPool.provision_sandbox/0 blocking the pool mailbox (unrelated module), ISS-0278 mentions unrelated design docs. None concerns the Ecto.Multi :task_records key collision. This is a first occurrence, not a recurrence -- severity stays as filed (MAJOR).

STEP 1 (root cause, independently confirmed against current lib/letflow/engine.ex and lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex on this branch -- not restated from ISS-0392.yaml's narrative):

TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/5 (lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex:250-258) always appends its step keyed {:task_records, instance_id} (fixed shape per instance_id, per its own doc comment at task_activation.ex:218-237 -- explicitly designed so calls for DIFFERENT instance_ids can coexist in one Multi, not so two calls for the SAME instance_id can).

Two call sites key this to the SAME parent_instance_id inside one transaction on the synchronous-completion path:

(1) engine.ex:2396-2476 build_complete_task_tail_multi/6 (the complete_task/3 hop-chain tail) computes parent_instance_id = normalized_changes.task.instance_id (line 2412), then at line 2414-2415 calls build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi(normalized_changes, completed_at, prefix) which (engine.ex:2572-2592) appends TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records(task.instance_id, ...) -- i.e. keyed {:task_records, parent_instance_id}. This step lands in the Multi FIRST, unconditionally, for every completion.

(2) The SAME build_complete_task_tail_multi/6, later in its own pipe chain (engine.ex:2461-2467), calls append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6 (engine.ex:2483-2502), which for each newly-prepared child calls SubProcess.append_start_multi/7 (sub_process.ex:398-479) onto the SAME accumulating Multi. append_start_multi/7 ends by calling maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6 (sub_process.ex:472-478). Its match clause fires ONLY when %{child_initial_state: %InstanceState{status: :completed}} (sub_process.ex:481-508) -- i.e. ONLY on the synchronous-completion path (a child graph like START->END with no intervening task reaches :completed inside prepare_child_activation/4 before any Multi step for it exists; a child with a pending HUMAN_TASK stays :active and this clause's sibling no-op clause at sub_process.ex:510-518 matches instead, appending nothing further -- this is exactly why the async/queued path never collides). When it fires, it calls SubProcess.append_completion_multi/5 (sub_process.ex:731-808) for the child against parent_token, whose parent_token.instance_id IS parent_instance_id from (1) (same hop chain, same parent). append_completion_multi/5 -> build_completion_multi_from_merge/12 -> build_completion_write_steps/12 (sub_process.ex:944-1011), which at lines 966-972 appends ANOTHER TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records(parent_instance_id, ...) call -- producing the IDENTICAL key {:task_records, parent_instance_id} already present in the same Multi from (1).

Ecto.Multi.merge/2's underlying merge_results/3 (ecto 3.14.1 lib/ecto/multi.ex:952) rejects the duplicate key at transaction-apply time, raising RuntimeError 'cannot merge Multi; the following operations were found in both Ecto.Multi: [task_records: \"<parent_instance_id>\"]', which Plug.Conn.WrapperError surfaces as a 500 -- exactly ISS-0392's filed symptom, confirmed verbatim by direct reproduction (see below), not merely re-read from the issue narrative.

Why only the synchronous path: on the async/queued path (child left :active with a pending HUMAN_TASK), maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6's no-op clause (sub_process.ex:510-518) returns the multi unchanged -- append_completion_multi/5 for that child is never called from inside THIS transaction at all; it only runs later, in a SEPARATE transaction, when that child's own task is independently completed via its own complete_task/3 call (a different top-level Multi, so no collision is possible there). The collision is structurally confined to the same-transaction chaining that only maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6's :completed clause triggers.

Why no existing test caught this: test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs's own graph_child_two_step/0 fixture (lines 119-136) carries an explicit comment at lines 119-120: 'Deliberately does NOT complete synchronously at creation time -- every test needs to observe the parent's waiting_child_instance_id/:waiting state'. Every SUB_PROCESS-completion test in that file and in test/letflow/engine/sub_process_test.exs (grepped both files for START->END-only child graphs / synchronous-completion scenarios: zero matches) builds its child around this same non-synchronous fixture, so maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6's :completed-match clause (the only branch that appends the colliding second TaskActivation call) is never exercised by the pre-existing suite. REQ-207's own simulation test (test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs) hit this defect during development and worked around it by using a pending HUMAN_TASK child instead of a synchronous START->END graph (documented in ISS-0392.yaml and in that test's own artifacts per REVIEWER's Step 2d note) -- so even that newer test does not cover the branch either, by deliberate workaround.

REPRODUCTION: wrote a throwaway ExUnit test, scratch/iss0392_repro_test.exs (git-ignored via /scratch/ in .gitignore; NOT committed, confirmed via `git status --porcelain scratch/` returning empty both before and after). It copies the exact fixture/call pattern from test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs's ISS-0067 describe block (graph_parent_task_then_subprocess_no_split/1: START->HUMAN_TASK('gate')->SUB_PROCESS('sp')->END, reached via a real Engine.complete_task/3 hop chain, matching REVIEWER's own note that these tests must exercise the real transaction shape), swapping only graph_child_two_step/0 (HUMAN_TASK child, non-synchronous) for a new graph_child_start_end/0 (plain START->END child, no task -- completes synchronously). Ran `mix test scratch/iss0392_repro_test.exs --seed 0`. Observed real output:

  1) test ISS-0392: completing the gate task, when the SUB_PROCESS child completes synchronously, raises Ecto.Multi key collision (Letflow.Iss0392ReproTest)
     scratch/iss0392_repro_test.exs:151
     ** (RuntimeError) cannot merge Multi; the following operations were found in both Ecto.Multi: [task_records: \"664242c4-1f8d-429f-a09e-7736483f7996\"]
     code: result = Engine.complete_task(gate_task.id, complete_attrs(), prefix: schema_name)
     stacktrace:
       (ecto 3.14.1) lib/ecto/multi.ex:952: Ecto.Multi.merge_results/3
       ...
       (letflow 0.1.0) lib/letflow/engine.ex:1594: Letflow.Engine.run_complete_task/6
       scratch/iss0392_repro_test.exs:172: (test)

This exactly matches ISS-0392.yaml's filed symptom (same error string, same key shape {task_records, <uuid>}), now independently reproduced against current source on this branch rather than trusted from the issue's own narrative.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE: the two TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records(parent_instance_id, ...) calls that can both land in one Multi for the same parent_instance_id -- (1) build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3's call at engine.ex:2584 (the hop chain's own unconditional parent-side task-activation step) and (2) build_completion_write_steps/12's call at sub_process.ex:966 (appended only via the maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6 -> append_completion_multi/5 chain when a child completes synchronously within the SAME transaction as its parent's own completion) -- must stop producing the same {:task_records, parent_instance_id} Multi key when both are present together in one transaction. CODE-DESIGNER owns the actual mechanism (e.g. making the second call idempotent/aware of the first's already-applied result, restructuring so only one of the two call sites performs task-activation for a given parent_instance_id per transaction, or keying/sequencing the two so they compose rather than collide) -- not prescribed here. Any design must also account for the grandparent cascade (maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6, sub_process.ex:1003-1010+) which can recurse this same append_completion_multi/5 -> build_completion_write_steps/12 path multiple times up an ancestor chain, each with its own distinct parent_instance_id (so those do NOT collide with each other, only each does/can collide with its own single hop-chain's unconditional activation call for the SAME instance_id).
